datapoint.context: I guess we are the only country in the world that does it? BT

qk_vs_ov_reading: mlp1 dwarfs every head by ~3 orders of magnitude (14.09 vs 0.012 max) -- the giant front token-table is doing essentially all the work of completing the acronym 'BTW'. Top-OV head 7.8 (ov=0.0119, qk=0.0015) is PAYLOAD-dominant (its value content matters, not where it looks) but numerically negligible. Top-QK head 10.5 (qk=0.0051 ~ ov=0.005) is in the SELECTION regime -- this is the known 10.5 'question head'; it shows up here but contributes almost nothing next to mlp1.
category_story: mlp1 ablation catastrophically raises CE (mean dCE=8.36 nats, hits 94% of all positions >0.5 nats) most on multi-token subword continuations of specific words/names and fixed repeated templates (e.g. 'Transferor spouse', form-blank '____', capitalized completions like 'BRU'->'CE') -- consistent with a broad token-identity/n-gram lookup table, not a narrow acronym-specific mechanism, even though this datapoint's target ('W' after 'BT') looks like exactly that category.
surprises: Known circuit 10.5 (question head) does appear as the top QK-regime head here, confirming its role, but its effect (0.005 nats) is utterly swamped by mlp1 (14.09 nats) -- for well-predicted acronym completions the specialized heads are essentially decorative next to the token-table.
